learning_objective: 🎯 Explore how media and technology connect the world, influence our thoughts, and serve as powerful tools for education and social change!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Communication is the process of sharing information, ideas, and feelings between a sender and a receiver. It requires a message and a medium (a channel) to travel through.
Media can be Print (newspapers, magazines), Broadcast (radio, television), or New/Digital Media (the internet, social media, smartphones). Each type has a different reach and speed.
Mass media reaches millions of people simultaneously. It plays a huge role in shaping public opinion, spreading awareness, providing entertainment, and educating the masses.
Satellites, fiber optics, and the internet have revolutionized communication. They have made the world a 'global village', allowing instant contact across continents.
While technology provides learning opportunities, overuse can lead to 'information overload', reduced physical activity, cyberbullying, and unrealistic body image expectations from social media.

fun_activity.title: 📵 The 2-Hour Disconnect
fun_activity.instructions: Try to turn off your phone and stay away from all screens for exactly 2 hours. Notice how many times you feel the urge to check a notification. It shows how deeply media technology is wired into our habits!

exam_tips: 📌 Distinguish between Print Media (static, requires literacy) and Broadcast Media (dynamic, accessible to illiterate populations).
📌 Be prepared to write about both the positive (education, awareness) and negative (addiction, misinformation) impacts of New Media.
📌 Remember that communication is a two-way process involving feedback.
quick_recap: ⭐ The internet is the fastest and most interactive form of mass media.
⭐ Media acts as the 'watchdog' of society by highlighting important issues.
⭐ Critical thinking is essential to filter out fake news in the digital age.
